candidates.title: Add gradient clipping and input validation to prevent NaN predictions
candidates.action: Use gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0) and add input validation (e.g., clamp inputs to valid range) to prevent NaN values in model outputs. Also ensure mixed precision training uses consistent autocast context and proper GradScaler usage.

candidates.title: Use multi-layer pooling (weighted average of last hidden layers) for transformer embeddings

candidates.title: Use consistent image dimensions across all samples in a batch to avoid DataLoader collation errors
candidates.action: Ensure all images in a batch have the same spatial dimensions by applying deterministic resizing or cropping after random augmentations, or by using a custom collate function that handles variable sizes.

candidates.title: Use XGBoost with standard squared error objective for fare prediction

candidates.title: Use multi-scale image feature extraction from SigLIP2 intermediate layers

candidates.title: Use stratified train/validation split to maintain class distribution

candidates.title: Use ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler for transformer fine-tuning to stabilize training

candidates.title: Use Logistic Regression as quick validation baseline

candidates.title: Use Exponential Moving Average (EMA) for model weights
candidates.action: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters during training and use the EMA model for validation and inference to improve generalization.

candidates.title: Ensure feature dimension matches model input dimension

candidates.title: Use EfficientNet-B3 with progressive resizing for improved generalization

candidates.title: Use MLP with engineered features and Sentence-BERT embeddings for baseline
candidates.action: Extract lexical, syntactic, stopword, structural, and char TF-IDF features, combine with Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2), and train a 3-layer MLP with LayerNorm, dropout, and AdamW. Use cosine annealing scheduler and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with standard AutoModelForSequenceClassification for strong performance
candidates.action: Use microsoft/deberta-v3-large with HuggingFace's AutoModelForSequenceClassification, CLS pooling, dropout, and linear classifier, fine-tuned with AdamW, cosine schedule, label smoothing, gradient clipping, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone with CutMix and MixUp for strong regularization
candidates.action: Use a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone from timm with a custom MLP classifier head. Apply CutMix (25% probability) and MixUp (25% probability) augmentations. candidates.title: Avoid progressive unfreezing that causes NaN losses due to optimizer re-initialization
candidates.action: If using progressive unfreezing, do not recreate the optimizer mid-training. Instead, adjust learning rates for different parameter groups before training starts, or use a single learning rate for all layers.

candidates.title: Use ModernBERT-large with TF-IDF and handcrafted features in a hybrid model for best performance
candidates.action: Combine ModernBERT-large fine-tuning with TF-IDF features (character 2-5-grams and word 1-3-grams) and handcrafted lexical/structural features (e.g., punctuation density, stop word rates, author-specific vocabulary counts). Fit TF-IDF vectorizers and StandardScaler per fold to prevent leakage. Use 3-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer, cosine LR schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and early stopping. This achieves log-loss around 0.35.

candidates.title: Avoid merge conflict markers in code files
candidates.action: Remove any merge conflict markers (e.g., '=======', '>>>>>>>') from the code before execution to prevent SyntaxError.

candidates.title: Use Focal Loss with label smoothing for imbalanced text classification
candidates.action: Use Focal Loss (gamma=2.0) combined with label smoothing (epsilon=0.1) to handle class imbalance and prevent overconfidence. Apply with AdamW optimizer and gradient clipping.

candidates.title: Use CalibratedClassifierCV with estimator parameter in newer scikit-learn
candidates.action: When using CalibratedClassifierCV from scikit-learn >=1.0, use the parameter name 'estimator' instead of 'base_estimator' or 'base_engine'.

candidates.title: Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation with ensemble averaging for robust predictions
candidates.action: Split training data into 5 stratified folds. For each fold, train a model on 4 folds and validate on the held-out fold, using early stopping to prevent overfitting. Average predictions from all folds for the test set.

candidates.title: Combine stylometric features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
candidates.action: Extract handcrafted stylometric features (punctuation density, sentence length, etc.) and concatenate with transformer pooled embeddings before classification.

candidates.title: Avoid leaving stray text comments outside of comment blocks in Python code
candidates.action: Ensure all explanatory text is inside comments (#) or docstrings. Remove any lines that are not valid Python code before execution.

candidates.title: Use CalibratedClassifierCV with estimator parameter instead of deprecated base_estimator
candidates.action: When using CalibratedClassifierCV from scikit-learn, pass the base model via the 'estimator' parameter, not the deprecated 'base_estimator' parameter.

candidates.title: Use AdaptiveFocalLoss with label smoothing for imbalanced classification
candidates.action: Use focal loss with adaptive gamma and label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration.

candidates.title: Define all variables and functions before use in training scripts
candidates.action: Ensure all variables, functions, and classes are defined before they are referenced in the code. This includes DataLoaders, datasets, model instances, and utility functions like cutmix.

candidates.title: Use label smoothing in CrossEntropyLoss to prevent overconfidence
candidates.action: Set CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1 to penalize overconfident predictions and improve generalization.

candidates.title: Use two-phase training: freeze backbone then fine-tune with discriminative learning rates
candidates.action: Train in two phases: Phase 1 freezes the transformer backbone and trains only the classification head and auxiliary modules; Phase 2 unfreezes the backbone (or LoRA adapters) with a lower learning rate to prevent overfitting and instability.

candidates.title: Use correct function for softplus activation: F.softplus instead of torch.softplus
candidates.action: Use torch.nn.functional.softplus (or F.softplus) for the softplus activation function, as torch.softplus does not exist.

candidates.title: Use SigLIP2 vision_model subcomponent for image-only feature extraction
candidates.action: When using SigLIP2 for image-only tasks, access the vision model via model_siglip.vision_model instead of the full model, to avoid requiring text inputs.

candidates.title: Combine stylometric features with transformer via cross-attention fusion
candidates.action: Engineer stylometric features (character/word counts, punctuation ratios, readability scores, etc.) and fuse them with transformer embeddings using a cross-attention module with gating to improve author identification.

candidates.title: Use XGBoost with standard squared error objective for fare prediction
candidates.action: Use 'reg:squarederror' objective for XGBoost instead of 'reg:pseudohubererror' to avoid divergence, and clip predictions before applying expm1 to prevent overflow.

candidates.title: Fit scaler/vectorizer on training fold only to prevent data leakage
candidates.action: When using per-fold feature scaling or vectorization, fit the scaler/vectorizer on the training fold only, then transform both training and validation folds. Do not use a pre-fitted scaler from outside the fold.

candidates.title: Avoid passing early_stopping_rounds to XGBClassifier.fit() in newer XGBoost versions
candidates.action: In newer XGBoost versions, do not pass 'early_stopping_rounds' as a parameter to fit(). Instead, use callbacks or the eval_set parameter with early_stopping_rounds in the XGBClassifier constructor.

candidates.title: Use DistilBERT with partial freezing and label smoothing for moderate performance
candidates.action: Freeze first 4 of 6 transformer layers, use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1, AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation, and mixed precision. Train with early stopping.

candidates.title: Use EfficientNet-B4 with CBAM attention and MixUp/CutMix for best performance
candidates.action: Use a pretrained EfficientNet-B4 backbone with a custom CBAM attention head and 3-layer MLP classifier. Apply RandAugment, RandomErasing, MixUp (80% probability), and CutMix (25% probability) augmentations. Train with Focal Loss with label smoothing, AdamW optimizer, OneCycleLR scheduler, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use test-time augmentation (horizontal flip) for final predictions.

candidates.title: Use attention pooling for sentence representation
candidates.action: Replace [CLS] token with a learned attention pooling layer: compute attention scores over all token embeddings via a learned query vector, apply softmax, and produce a weighted sum of token embeddings.

candidates.title: Combine handcrafted stylometric features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
candidates.action: Extract handcrafted features (e.g., text length, punctuation ratios, readability scores, POS approximations) and concatenate them with transformer embeddings (e.g., mean-pooled DeBERTa embeddings). Train an XGBoost classifier on the combined feature set to capture both linguistic and stylistic patterns.

candidates.title: Use direct feature concatenation instead of complex cross-attention fusion
candidates.action: Concatenate the [CLS] token embedding with projected engineered features (e.g., stylometric, TF-IDF) and pass through a simple MLP classifier. Avoid multi-head cross-attention or gated fusion mechanisms that introduce instability and overfitting.

candidates.title: Use correct DINOv2 input size (518x518) when using vit_large_patch14_dinov2
candidates.action: When using DINOv2 ViT-Large model from timm (vit_large_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m), resize input images to 518x518 as required by the model. Using smaller sizes (e.g., 224x224) will cause assertion errors.

candidates.title: Add gradient clipping and input validation to prevent NaN predictions
candidates.action: Use gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0) and add input validation (e.g., clamp inputs to valid range) to prevent NaN values in model outputs. Also ensure mixed precision training uses consistent autocast context and proper GradScaler usage.

candidates.title: Use correct indexing for StratifiedKFold splits
candidates.action: When using StratifiedKFold, ensure that the indices from split() are applied to the full dataset, not to a subset that has already been reduced in size, to avoid IndexError.

candidates.title: Use stratified K-fold cross-validation to ensure balanced validation splits
candidates.action: Use StratifiedKFold from sklearn to split the training data into folds that preserve the class distribution; use one fold for validation and the rest for training.

candidates.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with DistilBERT and CrossEntropyLoss for improved generalization
candidates.action: Use 5-fold StratifiedKFold cross-validation with DistilBERT, CrossEntropyLoss, AdamW optimizer, cosine schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation (2 steps), gradient clipping, mixed precision, and early stopping. Average test predictions across folds.

candidates.title: Use AdamW optimizer with weight decay for regularization
candidates.action: Use torch.optim.AdamW with weight_decay=1e-4 to apply decoupled weight decay, improving generalization.

candidates.title: Ensure model state_dict keys match when loading checkpoint
candidates.action: When saving and loading a custom model, ensure the architecture is identical at save and load time, or use strict=False and handle missing/unexpected keys appropriately.

candidates.title: Use mixed precision training with GradScaler for memory efficiency
candidates.action: Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) with torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler to reduce GPU memory usage and speed up training without significant accuracy loss.

candidates.title: Exclude non-numeric columns before filling NaNs with median
candidates.action: When filling missing values with the median, select only numeric columns to avoid TypeError on datetime or object columns.

candidates.title: Use float16-representable negative value in masked_fill
candidates.action: When using masked_fill with a large negative value (e.g., -1e9) in float16 (e.g., under AMP), use a value representable in float16 such as -1e4 or torch.finfo(torch.float16).min to prevent overflow errors.

candidates.title: Use XGBoost with hist tree method for CPU compatibility
candidates.action: Set XGBoost tree_method='hist' instead of 'gpu_hist' to avoid GPU compatibility issues, and move early_stopping_rounds to the constructor for older XGBoost versions.

candidates.title: Use temporal train/validation split to avoid data leakage
candidates.action: Split the data chronologically based on pickup datetime (e.g., 80% earliest for training, 20% latest for validation) to respect the time series nature of taxi trips.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of raw-fare and log-fare LightGBM models
candidates.action: Train two LightGBM models: one on raw fare and one on log-transformed fare, then ensemble their predictions (e.g., average) to handle the right-skewed fare distribution.

candidates.title: Use two-phase training with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning
candidates.action: Train in two phases: Phase 1 freezes all transformer layers and trains only the classification head for a few epochs; Phase 2 unfreezes selected layers (e.g., last 4-8) and fine-tunes with a lower learning rate. Use separate optimizers or parameter groups with differential learning rates.

candidates.title: Avoid using external GloVe embeddings that may not be available
candidates.action: Instead of relying on external GloVe embedding files (e.g., glove.6B.300d.txt) or torch.hub/torchtext GloVe loaders, use trainable random embeddings with Xavier initialization to avoid FileNotFoundError or download failures.

candidates.title: Avoid CatBoost random_seed and random_state conflict
candidates.action: When using CatBoostClassifier, do not set both 'random_seed' and 'random_state' parameters simultaneously. Use only 'random_state' for consistency.

candidates.title: Verify each sub-goal succeeds before proceeding in multi-stage pipelines
candidates.action: After each stage (feature extraction, model training, checkpoint saving, embedding extraction), print confirmation or check outputs. Ensure no silent failures before moving to next stage.

candidates.title: Use progressive unfreezing with discriminative learning rates and stochastic depth for transformer fine-tuning
candidates.action: Gradually unfreeze transformer layers from top to bottom, applying lower learning rates to lower layers. Use stochastic depth regularization on top layers. Train with AdamW optimizer, linear warmup, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use .loc instead of .iloc for boolean indexing
candidates.action: When filtering a DataFrame with a boolean mask, use .loc[mask] instead of .iloc[mask] because .iloc does not support boolean indexing.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with standard AutoModelForSequenceClassification for strong performance
candidates.action: Use microsoft/deberta-v3-large with HuggingFace's AutoModelForSequenceClassification, CLS pooling, dropout, and linear classifier, fine-tuned with AdamW, cosine schedule, label smoothing, gradient clipping, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use patch-based extraction with overlapping patches and weighted averaging reconstruction
candidates.action: Extract overlapping patches (e.g., 64x64 with stride 32) from full-resolution images, train on patches, and reconstruct full images by weighted averaging of overlapping predictions to preserve high-frequency details and avoid resolution loss.

candidates.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with ensemble averaging to improve generalization
candidates.action: Train separate models on each fold of a 5-fold stratified split and average their predictions (or use a meta-model) to reduce variance and improve test performance.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 with spatial attention for improved robustness
candidates.action: Create an ensemble of EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 models, each with a spatial attention module. Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation, RandAugment and CutMix augmentations, BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer with warmup and cosine annealing scheduler. Average predictions from all folds and both models for final submission.

candidates.title: Use CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts scheduler with linear warmup for transformer fine-tuning
candidates.action: Use a cosine annealing scheduler with linear warmup (e.g., warmup_steps=500) and restarts (T_0=10, T_mult=2) to improve generalization and escape plateaus.

candidates.title: Ensure test features dimension matches model input dimension
candidates.action: When creating test dataset tensors, verify that the number of test samples matches across all feature arrays (e.g., test_features, test_input_ids). Avoid computing test features on combined train+test data.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning and contrastive loss disabled
candidates.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with a classification head, disable contrastive loss to avoid NaN, use AdamW with linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and early stopping. Ensure checkpoint loading uses the exact saved filename.

candidates.title: Use AdamW optimizer with weight decay for transformer fine-tuning
candidates.action: Use AdamW from torch.optim with weight decay (e.g., 0.01) and separate parameter groups for bias and LayerNorm terms (no decay).

candidates.title: Use SigLIP2 vision transformer with two-stage fine-tuning for leaf classification
candidates.action: Use SigLIP2 (google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-256) as image feature extractor. In Stage 1, freeze SigLIP2 and train only an MLP classifier head. In Stage 2, fine-tune the last 2 transformer blocks of SigLIP2 along with the head using a lower learning rate. Use differential learning rates, label smoothing, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use focal loss with label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration
candidates.action: Replace standard cross-entropy with focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=None) combined with label smoothing (epsilon=0.1). This reduces the loss contribution from well-classified examples and prevents overconfidence.

candidates.title: Match model input dimension to actual feature dimension
candidates.action: Ensure the model's input dimension exactly matches the concatenated feature vector dimension. Compute the actual dimension after all feature extraction steps and set input_dim accordingly.

candidates.title: Use U-Net with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks and combined MSE+SSIM loss for denoising
candidates.action: Implement a U-Net autoencoder with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks in encoder/decoder, Gaussian noise injection, dropout, and skip connections. Train with a combined loss of MSE (or L1) and SSIM to improve perceptual quality and reduce RMSE.

candidates.title: Use mixed precision training with GradScaler for memory efficiency and speed
candidates.action: Use torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler to enable mixed precision training. Scale loss before backward and unscale gradients before clipping.

candidates.title: Use multi-sample dropout for improved generalization
candidates.action: Apply K forward passes with different dropout masks (K=4) and average the logits during training to regularize the model.

candidates.title: Download all required NLTK resources before tokenization
candidates.action: Download all necessary NLTK resources (punkt, averaged_perceptron_tagger, etc.) using nltk.download() before calling tokenization or POS tagging functions, and handle missing resources gracefully.

candidates.title: Use temporal ensemble of top-K checkpoints for transformer predictions
candidates.action: After fine-tuning, average the predicted probabilities from the top-K checkpoints (e.g., top 3 by validation log loss) using inverse log-loss weighting to stabilize predictions and improve calibration.

candidates.title: Use torch.load with weights_only=False for PyTorch 2.6+ compatibility
candidates.action: When loading model state_dicts saved with older PyTorch versions, set weights_only=False in torch.load to avoid PicklingError due to restricted pickle modules.

candidates.title: Use two-phase training: freeze backbone then full fine-tuning with discriminative learning rates
candidates.action: First train only the classifier head with the backbone frozen for a few epochs, then unfreeze the entire model and fine-tune with layer-wise learning rate decay (e.g., 1.0x for top layers, 0.95x per layer downward) to prevent overfitting.

candidates.title: Use TF-IDF n-gram features with character and word ranges
candidates.action: Extract character n-grams (2-7), word n-grams (1-3), and punctuation sequences using TfidfVectorizer; optionally combine with handcrafted features for downstream classifiers.

candidates.title: Use two-phase training with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning with proper device handling
candidates.action: When fine-tuning a transformer model, first train with frozen backbone for a few epochs, then unfreeze all parameters and continue training with a lower learning rate. Ensure all tensors are on the same device and use gradient clipping to avoid CUDA errors.

candidates.title: Use mean pooling of transformer hidden states instead of CLS token for better sentence representation
candidates.action: Apply mean pooling over all token hidden states from the last transformer layer (or last two layers) to obtain a fixed-size sentence embedding. Use this embedding as input to a classifier head.

candidates.title: Use logistic regression as a quick validation baseline and ensemble component
candidates.action: Train a multinomial logistic regression on sparse n-gram features (e.g., TF-IDF) as a fast baseline. Include its predictions in the final ensemble, often with a small weight.

candidates.title: Use semi-supervised test set augmentation for n-gram features
candidates.action: Append a fraction (e.g., 10%) of test samples with pseudo-labels to the training set before extracting n-gram TF-IDF features, improving domain adaptation for XGBoost.

candidates.title: Reduce gradient accumulation steps to lower peak memory
candidates.action: Use fewer gradient accumulation steps (e.g., 2 instead of 4) to reduce peak GPU memory usage during training.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with gradient checkpointing disabled and reduced batch size
candidates.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-small instead of large/base to fit in GPU memory. Disable gradient checkpointing to avoid backward pass errors, and reduce batch size to manage memory.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with multi-head attention pooling and multi-sample dropout
candidates.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with a multi-head attention pooling layer replacing CLS pooling, multi-sample dropout (4 forward passes averaged during training), layer-wise learning rate decay, label smoothing loss, gradient accumulation, mixed precision (AMP), and early stopping. Combine with 120 linguistic/stylistic features and TF-IDF vectors.

candidates.title: Use AdamW from torch.optim instead of transformers
candidates.action: Import AdamW from torch.optim (from torch.optim import AdamW) rather than from transformers to avoid ImportError due to version incompatibility in newer versions of transformers.

candidates.title: Avoid computing train AUC when mixup augmentation produces continuous labels
candidates.action: Skip computing training AUC when mixup augmentation is applied, as the continuous labels (floats between 0 and 1) are incompatible with roc_auc_score which expects binary labels. Only compute validation AUC on non-mixed batches.

candidates.title: Use correct classifier head dimensions for EfficientNet-V2-S backbone
candidates.action: When replacing the classifier head of EfficientNet-V2-S from timm, use the backbone's in_features attribute (e.g., 1280) for the first linear layer. Avoid adding extra pooling layers as the backbone already includes adaptive average pooling.

candidates.title: Use DistilBERT with focal loss and gradient accumulation for moderate performance
candidates.action: Use DistilBERT as the base model with focal loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, cosine schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation (steps=2), mixed precision training, and early stopping (patience=3). Use stratified train/validation split (80/20).

candidates.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues in Kaggle environments
candidates.action: Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader to avoid shared memory bus errors and worker crashes in restricted environments like Kaggle notebooks.

candidates.title: Use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing instead of LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy
candidates.action: Use torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss with the label_smoothing parameter instead of importing LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy from transformers, which may not be available.

candidates.title: Define all variables before use in script
candidates.action: Ensure all variables are defined before they are referenced, especially when using functions that return multiple values. Assign returned vectorizers, embeddings, etc. to named variables in the correct order.

candidates.title: Use early stopping with patience based on validation loss
candidates.action: Monitor validation loss and stop training if no improvement for a set number of epochs (e.g., patience=3); save the best model checkpoint.

candidates.title: Use DistilBERT with differential learning rates and gradual unfreezing
candidates.action: Freeze the first 4 layers of DistilBERT, fine-tune layers 4-5 with a lower learning rate (e.g., 2e-5), and use a higher learning rate (e.g., 2e-4) for the classification head. Optionally use two-phase training: freeze all transformer layers first, then unfreeze gradually.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of XGBoost, MLP on image features, and Logistic Regression with optimized weights
candidates.action: Train three models: XGBoost on engineered tabular features, an MLP on SigLIP2 image embeddings, and a Logistic Regression with polynomial features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss to minimize the metric.

candidates.title: Use smaller SentenceTransformer model to avoid CUDA OOM
candidates.action: Replace large SentenceTransformer models (e.g., all-mpnet-base-v2, 768-dim) with smaller ones (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) to reduce GPU memory usage and avoid CUDA out-of-memory errors during embedding extraction.

candidates.title: Avoid data augmentation that creates size mismatch between features and labels
candidates.action: When applying back-translation or other augmentation, ensure that the number of augmented samples matches the number of labels. Duplicate labels accordingly or use a dataset that handles augmentation internally.

candidates.title: Use Logistic Regression as quick validation baseline
candidates.action: Train a Logistic Regression on TF-IDF and handcrafted features to get a quick performance estimate before deep learning.

candidates.title: Use Vision Transformer (ViT) with partial unfreezing and MixUp for cactus classification
candidates.action: Use a pretrained ViT-Base/16 backbone from timm, unfreeze the last 6 transformer blocks, and add a custom MLP classifier head. Apply MixUp augmentation (50% probability). Use differential learning rates (backbone 1e-5, head 3e-4), AdamW optimizer, cosine annealing scheduler, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use test-time augmentation (horizontal flip averaging) for final predictions.

candidates.title: Avoid using torch.no_grad() inside autocast() when gradients are needed
candidates.action: Do not wrap operations that require gradients with torch.no_grad() inside an autocast context. If MixUp or similar augmentation requires no_grad, compute it outside the training loop or on logits after forward pass.

candidates.title: Avoid rebuilding optimizer mid-training to prevent memory leaks
candidates.action: Do not recreate the optimizer or scheduler during training (e.g., at progressive unfreezing stages). Instead, update parameter groups in-place or use a single optimizer throughout.

candidates.title: Use correct attribute path for HuggingFace model layers
candidates.action: For DistilRoBERTa, access layers via model.roberta.encoder.layer. For DeBERTa-v3, access via model.deberta.encoder.layer. Verify the correct attribute path for the specific model variant.

candidates.title: Use correct indexing for EfficientNet backbone blocks when unfreezing
candidates.action: When unfreezing specific blocks of an EfficientNet backbone from timm, iterate over the blocks list and unfreeze the last N blocks by index (e.g., for EfficientNet-B0, blocks are indexed 0-6, so unfreeze blocks[4:] for last 3 blocks). Use len(backbone.blocks) to determine the total number of blocks.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with mean pooling and simple MLP classifier for stable fine-tuning
candidates.action: Load DeBERTa-v3-base with AutoModel (not AutoModelForSequenceClassification). Apply mean pooling over token embeddings (excluding padding). Add a 2-layer MLP classifier (e.g., hidden size 256) with dropout. Train with cross-entropy loss (label smoothing 0.1), AdamW (lr 2e-5), cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. Use early stopping on validation log-loss.

candidates.title: Ensure SSIM loss tensor dtype matches model input dtype under mixed precision
candidates.action: Create the Gaussian window for SSIM loss with the same dtype as the input tensors (e.g., using .type_as()) to avoid dtype mismatch when using autocast (AMP).

candidates.title: Define all functions and variables before use in script
candidates.action: Ensure all custom functions (e.g., extract_stylometric_features) and variables are defined before they are called, and avoid forward references.

candidates.title: Use DINOv2 ViT-S/14 encoder with trainable backbone and differential learning rates
candidates.action: Use a pretrained DINOv2 ViT-S/14 as encoder, with a small warmup LR for the backbone (e.g., linear warmup from 0 to 5e-5) and a higher LR for the decoder (e.g., 1e-3), and unfreeze the last few encoder blocks after warmup.

candidates.title: Move loss function weights to same device as input tensors
candidates.action: Ensure all buffers in custom loss functions (e.g., AdaptiveFocalLoss.weights) are moved to the same device as the input tensors.

candidates.title: Use smaller model variant to avoid CUDA OOM
candidates.action: When encountering CUDA out-of-memory errors, switch to a smaller model variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small or ModernBERT-base instead of DeBERTa-v3-large or ModernBERT-large) and reduce batch size (e.g., batch_size=8), max sequence length (e.g., max_length=256), and gradient accumulation steps to fit GPU memory.

candidates.title: Avoid calling scaler.unscale_ twice per step
candidates.action: Call scaler.unscale_(optimizer) only once per gradient accumulation step, and not before FGM attack if scaler.step will call it automatically, to prevent RuntimeError.

candidates.title: Use early stopping based on validation log loss to prevent overfitting
candidates.action: Monitor validation log loss each epoch and stop training if it does not improve for a patience number of epochs (e.g., 30), restoring the best model weights.

candidates.title: Use single-phase training instead of progressive unfreezing to avoid OOM
candidates.action: Train the entire model from the start with a lower learning rate for the backbone, avoiding progressive unfreezing which can cause memory spikes when unfreezing layers.

candidates.title: Use ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone with CutMix and MixUp for strong regularization
candidates.action: Use a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone from timm with a custom MLP classifier head. Apply CutMix (25% probability) and MixUp (25% probability) augmentations. Use AdamW optimizer with differential learning rates (backbone 5e-5, head 1e-3), warmup cosine annealing scheduler, label smoothing BCE loss, gradient clipping, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss
candidates.action: After training individual models, perform a grid search over weight combinations (e.g., step 0.05) to minimize validation log loss, then apply the optimal weights to test predictions.

candidates.title: Use correct file path for training data and avoid hardcoded local paths
candidates.action: Use relative paths or environment variables to locate data files (e.g., './input/train.csv') instead of hardcoded absolute paths that may not exist in the execution environment.

candidates.title: Ensure labels are float type for BCEWithLogitsLoss
candidates.action: Convert target labels to float type (e.g., batch_y.float()) before passing to BCEWithLogitsLoss, as it expects float targets. Avoid using Long type which can cause type mismatch errors.

candidates.title: Ensure OOF prediction arrays have consistent shapes across folds
candidates.action: When assembling out-of-fold predictions, ensure each fold's validation predictions are placed at the correct indices in a pre-allocated array of shape (n_samples, n_classes). Do not stack arrays of different sizes.

candidates.title: Use DistilRoBERTa with 5-fold cross-validation and cosine warmup scheduler for text classification
candidates.action: Use DistilRoBERTa (distilroberta-base) with a classification head. Train with 5-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer (learning_rate=2e-5), cosine schedule with warmup (warmup_steps=500), gradient accumulation (2 steps), mixed precision via Accelerator, early stopping (patience=3) based on validation log loss. Tokenize with max_length=256.

candidates.title: Use attention gates in U-Net skip connections for denoising
candidates.action: Add attention gates (e.g., additive attention) to the skip connections of a U-Net to suppress irrelevant features and enhance important spatial regions, improving denoising quality.

candidates.title: Use torch.save(model.state_dict(), ...) and load with model.load_state_dict(...) to avoid pooler mismatch
candidates.action: Save only the state_dict (not the full model) and load it into the model instance. Ensure the model architecture (including pooler) is consistent between save and load. For DeBERTa, avoid expecting a pooler layer if using AutoModelForSequenceClassification.

candidates.title: Avoid scaling categorical features with StandardScaler
candidates.action: Separate categorical features from numerical features before scaling; apply StandardScaler only to numerical columns to prevent negative values in categorical features that LightGBM cannot handle.

candidates.title: Ensure attention mask shape matches multi-head attention expectations
candidates.action: When using nn.MultiheadAttention with num_heads > 1, expand the attention mask to shape [batch_size * num_heads, seq_len, seq_len] instead of [batch_size, seq_len, seq_len].

candidates.action: Load DeBERTa-v3-base with AutoModel (not AutoModelForSequenceClassification). Apply mean pooling over token embeddings (excluding padding). Add a 2-layer MLP classifier (e.g., hidden size 256) with dropout. Train with cross-entropy loss (label smoothing 0.1), AdamW (lr 2e-5), cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. Use early stopping on validation log-loss.

candidates.title: Ensure classifier input dimension matches actual concatenated feature dimension
candidates.action: When building multi-encoder models, compute the total feature dimension by running a dummy forward pass or carefully summing encoder output dimensions. Verify that the classifier's first linear layer input size matches the actual concatenated feature size.

candidates.title: Avoid passing dropout params directly to from_pretrained
candidates.action: Do not pass 'hidden_dropout_prob' or 'attention_probs_dropout_prob' as keyword arguments to from_pretrained(). Instead, modify the model's configuration after loading or use a config object. Passing these directly causes a TypeError.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with mean pooling, multi-sample dropout, and Focal Loss for robust text classification
candidates.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-large backbone with mean pooling of hidden states, multi-sample dropout (4 samples), and a simple linear classifier head. Train with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping, linear warmup, and ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler. Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation and early stopping.

candidates.title: Clean merged or generated code before execution
candidates.action: Before execution, remove merge markers, stray prose, duplicated definitions, Markdown/HTML fragments, and other non-Python artifacts.

candidates.title: Define all variables and DataLoaders before they are used in the script
candidates.action: Ensure that every variable, DataLoader, and function is defined earlier in the script than its first usage, especially in multi-stage pipelines where later stages depend on earlier ones.

candidates.title: Escape regex special characters in str.count for parenthesis counting
candidates.action: When counting parentheses in text using str.count, use literal strings (e.g., '(' and ')') as str.count does not interpret regex. However, if using regex functions like re.findall, escape parentheses with backslash. In pandas, str.count with '(' works correctly as it treats the argument as a literal string, not a regex pattern.

candidates.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues in Kaggle environments
candidates.action: Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader to avoid shared memory bus errors and worker crashes in restricted environments like Kaggle notebooks.

candidates.title: Ensure EMA shadow dictionary is updated when adding new parameters
candidates.action: After progressive unfreezing adds new trainable parameters, re-register EMA to include the new parameters in the shadow dictionary.

candidates.title: Use correct indexing for EfficientNet backbone blocks when unfreezing
candidates.action: When unfreezing specific blocks of an EfficientNet backbone from timm, iterate over the blocks list and unfreeze the last N blocks by index (e.g., for EfficientNet-B0, blocks are indexed 0-6, so unfreeze blocks[4:] for last 3 blocks). Use len(backbone.blocks) to determine the total number of blocks.

candidates.title: Use temporal ensemble of top-K checkpoints for transformer predictions
candidates.action: After fine-tuning, average the predicted probabilities from the top-K checkpoints (e.g., top 3 by validation log loss) using inverse log-loss weighting to stabilize predictions and improve calibration.

candidates.title: Ensure test image paths are correctly handled during pseudo-labeling retraining
candidates.action: When adding pseudo-labeled test samples to the training set, ensure the dataset loader can access images from both train and test directories. Either copy test images to the train directory or modify the dataset to accept a list of image paths with corresponding directories.

candidates.title: Use TF-IDF n-gram features with character and word ranges
candidates.action: Extract character n-grams (2-7), word n-grams (1-3), and punctuation sequences using TfidfVectorizer; optionally combine with handcrafted features for downstream classifiers.

candidates.title: Use EfficientNet-B4 with CBAM attention and MixUp/CutMix for best performance
candidates.action: Use a pretrained EfficientNet-B4 backbone with a custom CBAM attention head and 3-layer MLP classifier. Apply RandAugment, RandomErasing, MixUp (80% probability), and CutMix (25% probability) augmentations. Train with Focal Loss with label smoothing, AdamW optimizer, OneCycleLR scheduler, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use test-time augmentation (horizontal flip) for final predictions.

candidates.title: Avoid passing early_stopping_rounds to XGBClassifier.fit() in newer XGBoost versions
candidates.action: In newer XGBoost versions, do not pass 'early_stopping_rounds' as a parameter to fit(). Instead, use callbacks or the eval_set parameter with early_stopping_rounds in the XGBClassifier constructor.

candidates.title: Avoid using external GloVe embeddings that may not be available
candidates.action: Instead of relying on external GloVe embedding files (e.g., glove.6B.300d.txt) or torch.hub/torchtext GloVe loaders, use trainable random embeddings with Xavier initialization to avoid FileNotFoundError or download failures.

candidates.title: Use text augmentation (word swaps, punctuation insertion, vowel noise, synonym replacement) to reduce overfitting
candidates.action: Apply balanced text augmentations to training samples: random word swaps within a window, random punctuation insertion, vowel noise (replace vowels), and synonym replacement using WordNet.

candidates.title: Use direct feature concatenation instead of complex cross-attention fusion
candidates.action: Concatenate the [CLS] token embedding with projected engineered features (e.g., stylometric, TF-IDF) and pass through a simple MLP classifier. Avoid multi-head cross-attention or gated fusion mechanisms that introduce instability and overfitting.

candidates.title: Avoid CatBoost random_seed and random_state conflict
candidates.action: When using CatBoostClassifier, do not set both 'random_seed' and 'random_state' parameters simultaneously. Use only 'random_state' for consistency.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of DeBERTa-v3-large, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression with weight optimization
candidates.action: Combine predictions from fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large (with label smoothing, early stopping, mixed precision), XGBoost trained on DeBERTa embeddings plus handcrafted features, and Logistic Regression on TF-IDF n-gram features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss.

candidates.title: Avoid data leakage by fitting PCA and scalers on training fold only
candidates.action: When performing dimensionality reduction (PCA) or scaling, fit the transformation on the training fold only, then transform validation and test sets using the fitted object. Do not fit separately on each split.

candidates.title: Use correct attribute name for ModernBERT embedding layer
candidates.action: Access ModernBERT's embedding layer via model.model.embeddings.tok_embeddings, not word_embeddings.

candidates.title: Use handcrafted stylometric features for authorship attribution
candidates.action: Extract 26 stylometric features including word-level statistics (avg word length, sentence length), punctuation density, stopword ratio, type-token ratio, readability indices (Coleman-Lieu, Flesch), lexical richness measures, and normalize with StandardScaler.

candidates.title: Use .loc instead of .iloc for boolean indexing
candidates.action: When filtering a DataFrame with a boolean mask, use .loc[mask] instead of .iloc[mask] because .iloc does not support boolean indexing.

candidates.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues in containerized environments
candidates.action: Set num_workers=0 and pin_memory=False in DataLoader to avoid shared memory (shm) exhaustion, which causes bus errors and worker crashes. This trades off data loading speed for reliability.

candidates.title: Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost
candidates.action: Extract [CLS] embeddings from multiple frozen transformers (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, DistilBERT-base), concatenate them, and train an XGBoost classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use correct attribute path for ModernBERT backbone layers
candidates.action: ModernBERT uses 'encoder.layer' (not 'transformer.layers' or 'encoder.layer' may vary; check model config). Access layers via model.backbone.encoder.layer or model.encoder.layer depending on the model wrapper.

candidates.title: Use CalibratedClassifierCV with estimator parameter instead of deprecated base_estimator
candidates.action: When using CalibratedClassifierCV from scikit-learn, pass the base model via the 'estimator' parameter, not the deprecated 'base_estimator' parameter.

candidates.title: Use correct classifier head dimensions for EfficientNet-V2-S backbone
candidates.action: When replacing the classifier head of EfficientNet-V2-S from timm, use the backbone's in_features attribute (e.g., 1280) for the first linear layer. Avoid adding extra pooling layers as the backbone already includes adaptive average pooling.

candidates.title: Use noise prior input channel (median filter residual) to improve denoising
candidates.action: Compute a noise prior map as the residual between the noisy image and its median-filtered version, and stack it as an additional input channel (e.g., 2-channel input) to provide explicit noise information to the model.

candidates.title: Use AdaptiveFocalLoss with label smoothing for imbalanced classification
candidates.action: Use focal loss with adaptive gamma and label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration.

candidates.title: Use AdamW from torch.optim instead of transformers
candidates.action: Import AdamW from torch.optim (from torch.optim import AdamW) rather than from transformers to avoid ImportError due to version incompatibility in newer versions of transformers.

candidates.title: Use gradient clipping to stabilize training and avoid NaN losses
candidates.action: Apply torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0) after loss.backward() to prevent gradient explosion.

candidates.title: Clip probabilities after softmax to avoid NaN in log_loss
candidates.action: After computing softmax probabilities, clip them to a small epsilon range (e.g., 1e-7, 1-1e-7) to avoid log(0) and NaN values when computing log loss.

candidates.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues
candidates.action: Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader (and optionally pin_memory=False) to prevent 'No space left on device' or CUDA bus errors caused by limited shared memory (/dev/shm) in containerized environments.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with 3-fold cross-validation and early stopping for strong performance
candidates.action: Use AutoModelForSequenceClassification with 'microsoft/deberta-v3-base', max_length=256, 3-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler with warmup, CrossEntropyLoss, and early stopping (patience=2). Average predictions across folds, clip and normalize. This achieves log-loss around 0.38 on the spooky-author-identification task.

candidates.title: Use XGBoost with handcrafted stylometric features and Sentence-BERT embeddings for text classification
candidates.action: Combine 32 handcrafted stylometric features (text statistics, punctuation ratios, POS-like patterns, emotional tone indicators) with 384-dimensional Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Scale features with StandardScaler. Train XGBoost with multi:softprob objective, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1, n_estimators=500, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, early_stopping_rounds=50, using 5-fold stratified cross-validation.

candidates.title: Use torch.save(model.state_dict(), ...) and load with model.load_state_dict(...) to avoid pooler mismatch
candidates.action: Save only the state_dict (not the full model) and load it into the model instance. Ensure the model architecture (including pooler) is consistent between save and load. For DeBERTa, avoid expecting a pooler layer if using AutoModelForSequenceClassification.

candidates.title: Use consistent variable names to avoid NameError
candidates.action: Ensure that variable names used in code are defined and spelled consistently. Avoid referencing undefined variables or using different suffixes (e.g., test_features vs test_features_fold).

candidates.title: Use two-stage fine-tuning with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning
candidates.action: First train only the classifier head and gating network with frozen backbone for a few epochs, then unfreeze all layers for full fine-tuning. This prevents overfitting and improves generalization.

candidates.title: Avoid FGM adversarial training with torch.compile or retain_graph=True
candidates.action: Remove FGM adversarial training or ensure backward passes do not use retain_graph=True when using torch.compile.

candidates.title: Use SigLIP2 vision_model subcomponent for image-only feature extraction
candidates.action: When using SigLIP2 for image-only tasks, access the vision model via model_siglip.vision_model instead of the full model, to avoid requiring text inputs.

candidates.title: Avoid data augmentation that creates size mismatch between features and labels
candidates.action: When applying back-translation or other augmentation, ensure that the number of augmented samples matches the number of labels. Duplicate labels accordingly or use a dataset that handles augmentation internally.

candidates.title: Use CosineAnnealingLR scheduler with warmup for stable training
candidates.action: Implement a cosine annealing learning rate schedule with a linear warmup phase (e.g., 5 epochs) to gradually increase LR then decay, helping convergence.

candidates.title: Use penalty=None instead of penalty='none' in scikit-learn LogisticRegression
candidates.action: When initializing LogisticRegression with no penalty, set penalty=None (Python None), not the string 'none'. The string 'none' is invalid and causes an InvalidParameterError.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with ensemble of XGBoost and Logistic Regression for best performance
candidates.action: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-large with AdamW, linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient clipping, label smoothing, and early stopping. Combine its embeddings with engineered features (stylometric, readability, POS, n-grams) and train XGBoost and Logistic Regression, then optimize ensemble weights via validation log loss.

candidates.title: Use single-phase training instead of progressive unfreezing to avoid OOM
candidates.action: Train the entire model from the start with a lower learning rate for the backbone, avoiding progressive unfreezing which can cause memory spikes when unfreezing layers.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning and contrastive loss disabled
candidates.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with a classification head, disable contrastive loss to avoid NaN, use AdamW with linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and early stopping. Ensure checkpoint loading uses the exact saved filename.

candidates.title: Use DistilRoBERTa with weighted averaging of last 4 hidden states and deep classification head
candidates.action: Use DistilRoBERTa backbone with weighted average of last 4 hidden states, mean pooling, and a deep classification head with LayerNorm and dropout. Train with CrossEntropyLoss with label smoothing, AdamW optimizer, mixed precision, and gradient clipping.

candidates.title: Disable gradient checkpointing when using gradient accumulation
candidates.action: Disable gradient_checkpointing_enable() when using gradient accumulation with AMP, as it causes 'Trying to backward through the graph a second time' errors. Instead, reduce batch size to manage memory.

candidates.title: Use correct indexing for StratifiedKFold splits
candidates.action: When using StratifiedKFold, ensure that the indices from split() are applied to the full dataset, not to a subset that has already been reduced in size, to avoid IndexError.

candidates.title: Avoid two-stage residual boosting for taxi fare prediction
candidates.action: Single-stage LightGBM with proper regularization outperforms two-stage residual boosting, which provides negligible improvement and risks overfitting.

candidates.title: Use EfficientNet-B0 with end-to-end fine-tuning and CutMix augmentation for cactus classification
candidates.action: Use a pretrained EfficientNet-B0 backbone from timm, fine-tune end-to-end with BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer (backbone lr=5e-5, head lr=1e-3), warmup cosine annealing scheduler, CutMix augmentation (50% probability per batch), gradient clipping, and early stopping based on validation AUC.

candidates.title: Avoid duplicate parameter groups in optimizer
candidates.action: Ensure that no parameter appears in more than one parameter group when creating the optimizer, by using set operations or careful grouping, to avoid ValueError.

candidates.title: Use consistent variable names to avoid NameError from undefined variables
candidates.action: After feature engineering, ensure the variable names used for training data (e.g., X_train, y_train) match those used in subsequent steps. Avoid referencing variables like X_train_fold that were never defined.

candidates.title: Define all functions and variables before use in script
candidates.action: Ensure all custom functions (e.g., extract_stylometric_features) and variables are defined before they are called, and avoid forward references.

candidates.title: Handle missing values per feature group with median imputation to avoid data leakage
candidates.action: Impute missing values separately for each feature group (margin, shape, texture) using SimpleImputer(strategy='median') fitted on the training fold only, to prevent leakage from validation data.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of raw-fare and log-fare LightGBM models
candidates.action: Train two LightGBM models: one on raw fare and one on log-transformed fare, then ensemble their predictions (e.g., average) to handle the right-skewed fare distribution.

candidates.title: Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation with OOF predictions for robust ensemble
candidates.action: Implement 5-fold stratified cross-validation to generate out-of-fold (OOF) predictions from each model, then train a meta-learner (e.g., logistic regression) on OOF probabilities to learn ensemble weights. This reduces overfitting and improves generalization compared to a single train/validation split.

candidates.title: Use focal loss with label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration
candidates.action: Replace standard cross-entropy with focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=None) combined with label smoothing (epsilon=0.1). This reduces the loss contribution from well-classified examples and prevents overconfidence.

candidates.title: Use LightGBM meta-classifier on transformer embeddings and handcrafted features
candidates.action: After training a transformer (e.g., RoBERTa, DeBERTa), extract pooled embeddings from the best checkpoint. Concatenate with handcrafted features (stylometric, readability, POS, n-gram TF-IDF). Train a LightGBM classifier on the combined features using the validation set. Use the LightGBM predictions as a meta-learner to improve ensemble performance.

candidates.title: Avoid passing label_smoothing parameter to BCEWithLogitsLoss in older PyTorch versions
candidates.action: Check PyTorch version before using label_smoothing with BCEWithLogitsLoss. If version < 1.10, implement label smoothing manually or use standard BCEWithLogitsLoss without label_smoothing.

candidates.title: Ensure SSIM loss tensor dtype matches model input dtype under mixed precision
candidates.action: Create the Gaussian window for SSIM loss with the same dtype as the input tensors (e.g., using .type_as()) to avoid dtype mismatch when using autocast (AMP).

candidates.title: Use CPU tensors for model checkpoint saving to avoid file write errors
candidates.action: When saving model checkpoints, move tensors to CPU first (model.to('cpu')) to avoid file write errors that can occur with GPU tensors in multi-worker settings.

candidates.title: Use Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) to improve generalization
candidates.action: After training, average model weights from the last few epochs (e.g., last 5) using SWA to obtain a smoother solution that generalizes better.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of DeBERTa-v3-large, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression with optimized weights
candidates.action: Train DeBERTa-v3-large with label smoothing (0.1), linear warmup scheduler, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. Extract pooled embeddings and combine with handcrafted stylometric/readability/POS features. Train XGBoost and Logistic Regression on concatenated features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search (e.g., DeBERTa=0.1, XGBoost=0.8, LogisticRegression=0.1) to minimize validation log-loss.

candidates.title: Use handcrafted features combined with CNN features for robust classification
candidates.action: Extract handcrafted features (color histograms, GLCM texture, LBP, edge features, statistical features, HOG, pooled grayscale) and combine with CNN features from a pretrained EfficientNet-V2-S. Standardize features with StandardScaler and train an MLP classifier with BatchNorm, ReLU, and dropout.

candidates.title: Use TF-IDF with handcrafted features and Logistic Regression as a strong baseline for text classification
candidates.action: Combine TF-IDF vectorization (max 50k features, 1-3 ngrams) with handcrafted statistical features (character/word/sentence counts, punctuation counts, quote density, capital ratio, unique word ratio, stopword ratio). Scale features with StandardScaler and concatenate via sparse hstack. Train a multinomial Logistic Regression (C=4.0, solver='saga') with 5-fold stratified cross-validation. This provides a robust baseline that avoids overfitting on small datasets.

candidates.title: Use extensive tabular feature engineering with statistical summaries, ratios, correlations, and PCA for leaf classification
candidates.action: Engineer tabular features from margin/shape/texture groups: per-group statistics (mean, std, min, max, skew, kurtosis, quartiles, IQR, range, CV), ratio features, cross-group correlations, PCA per group (8 components) and difference PCA (5 components). Fit all transformations on the training fold only to prevent leakage.

candidates.title: Avoid NaN predictions by simplifying attention mechanisms and using gradient clipping
candidates.action: When using complex attention pooling (e.g., weighted layer attention, multi-head attention) with mixed precision, simplify architecture or add gradient clipping (norm=1.0) and torch.nan_to_num to prevent NaN outputs.

candidates.title: Avoid complex multi-task losses (contrastive, center loss) that cause dimension mismatches
candidates.action: Stick to simple cross-entropy or focal loss with label smoothing. If using additional losses, ensure embedding dimensions match exactly (e.g., projection head output dim equals centers dim).

candidates.title: Use ensemble of DistilBERT, XGBoost on TF-IDF, and CharCNN-LSTM
candidates.action: Combine predictions from a fine-tuned DistilBERT, an XGBoost model trained on TF-IDF + stylistic features, and a character-level CNN-LSTM, weighted by validation performance. This ensemble breaks plateaus.

candidates.title: Ensure DataLoader objects are defined before use in training loops
candidates.action: After feature engineering and dataset creation, explicitly create DataLoader objects (train_loader, val_loader, etc.) before entering the training loop. Verify all loader variables are defined.

candidates.title: Define all classes and functions before their first use in the script
candidates.action: Order code so that class and function definitions appear before any instantiation or call. For test datasets, define the dataset class before creating test loaders.

candidates.title: Use multi-branch MLP with per-group branches and cross-attention fusion
candidates.action: Design a neural network with separate MLP branches for each feature group (e.g., margin, shape, texture), then fuse via cross-attention mechanism followed by a classifier head. Use moderate dropout (0.3) and batch normalization.

candidates.title: Use multi-pooling head (CLS, mean, max, attention) with gated fusion
candidates.action: Combine CLS, mean, max, and attention-weighted pooling via a learned gating mechanism to create a richer sentence representation.

candidates.title: Use DINOv2 ViT-L/14 with gated multimodal fusion for leaf classification
candidates.action: Use DINOv2 ViT-L/14 as frozen image feature extractor (1024-dim), engineer extensive tabular features (raw values, per-group statistics, cross-group interactions, PCA), and train a multimodal classifier with separate projectors for tabular and image modalities, a learnable gating fusion mechanism, and a classifier head with label smoothing cross-entropy loss. Use AdamW optimizer with cosine annealing scheduler, mixed precision training, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Handle None pooler in RoBERTa for layer grouping
candidates.action: When implementing gradual unfreezing or discriminative learning rates for RoBERTa, check if `model.roberta.pooler` is None before accessing its parameters. If None, exclude it from the parameter groups.

candidates.title: Use ensemble of XGBoost, MLP on image features, and Logistic Regression with optimized weights
candidates.action: Train three models: XGBoost on engineered tabular features, an MLP on SigLIP2 image embeddings, and a Logistic Regression with polynomial features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss to minimize the metric.

candidates.title: Pass all required arguments to function calls to avoid TypeError
candidates.action: Ensure that when calling a function, all required positional arguments are provided. Check function signature and call site for missing arguments.

candidates.title: Ensure model forward method returns logits consistently for evaluation
candidates.action: Define model forward to return a tuple (logits, pooled) or a single tensor. Ensure evaluate() function unpacks the correct number of outputs. Avoid multiple evaluate() definitions that expect different return signatures.

candidates.title: Compute group statistics on training fold only to prevent data leakage
candidates.action: Compute location-based group statistics (mean, std, count) only on the training portion after splitting, not on the full dataset before split, to avoid leaking validation information.

candidates.title: Avoid random truncation strategies that corrupt sentence structure
candidates.action: Use consistent truncation (e.g., 'head' or 'tail') instead of random truncation to prevent tokenization issues and numerical instability that lead to NaN predictions.

candidates.title: Use cosine annealing scheduler with warmup for transformer fine-tuning
candidates.action: Use torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR or OneCycleLR with linear warmup to gradually decrease learning rate, improving convergence.

candidates.title: Avoid data leakage by fitting scalers and PCA on training fold only
candidates.action: Within each cross-validation fold, fit StandardScaler and PCA exclusively on the training subset, then transform both train and validation subsets. Never use the full dataset before splitting.

candidates.title: Use ModernBERT-large with proper dropout configuration via config object
candidates.action: Load ModernBertForSequenceClassification without dropout kwargs, then set dropout via model.config.hidden_dropout_prob and model.config.attention_probs_dropout_prob after loading.

candidates.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with MiniLM transformer and sparse features
candidates.action: Train a MiniLM transformer fused with sparse TF-IDF and stylistic features using 5-fold cross-validation, averaging predictions across folds for better generalization.

candidates.title: Use torch.load with weights_only=False for PyTorch 2.6+ compatibility
candidates.action: When loading model state_dicts saved with older PyTorch versions, set weights_only=False in torch.load to avoid PicklingError due to restricted pickle modules.

candidates.title: Fit scaler/vectorizer on training fold only to prevent data leakage
candidates.action: When using per-fold feature scaling or vectorization, fit the scaler/vectorizer on the training fold only, then transform both training and validation folds. Do not use a pre-fitted scaler from outside the fold.

candidates.title: Use correct file path for training data
candidates.action: Read training data from './input/labels.csv' instead of './input/train.csv' when the dataset uses a different filename.

candidates.title: Use correct attribute path for HuggingFace model backbone layers
candidates.action: Access backbone layers via the correct attribute name (e.g., model.backbone for ModernBERT, model.dinov2 for DINOv2) to avoid AttributeError when building custom heads.

candidates.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with multi-head attention pooling and multi-sample dropout
candidates.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with a multi-head attention pooling layer replacing CLS pooling, multi-sample dropout (4 forward passes averaged during training), layer-wise learning rate decay, label smoothing loss, gradient accumulation, mixed precision (AMP), and early stopping. Combine with 120 linguistic/stylistic features and TF-IDF vectors.

candidates.title: Avoid overlapping parameter groups in optimizer construction
candidates.action: Ensure that parameter groups for differential learning rates are mutually exclusive. Use set operations to verify no parameter appears in multiple groups before creating the optimizer.

candidates.title: Use MLP with engineered features and Sentence-BERT embeddings for baseline
candidates.action: Extract lexical, syntactic, stopword, structural, and char TF-IDF features, combine with Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2), and train a 3-layer MLP with LayerNorm, dropout, and AdamW. Use cosine annealing scheduler and early stopping.

candidates.title: Ensure stylometric feature array index matches DataFrame index after train/validation split
candidates.action: When creating stylometric feature arrays from a DataFrame, use .iloc or .loc with the validation indices derived from the DataFrame's index, or reset the DataFrame index before splitting to avoid index mismatch. Alternatively, fit the feature scaler on the training fold and transform both folds using integer-based indexing.

candidates.title: Use TF-IDF features with n-grams up to 3
candidates.action: Extract character n-grams (2-5) and word n-grams (1-3) using TF-IDF vectorization, limiting to 500-1000 features. Fit the vectorizer on the training fold only to prevent data leakage.

candidates.title: Use consistent tensor dimensions in pooling operations
candidates.action: When applying pooling (mean, max) to LSTM or transformer outputs, ensure the mask tensor has the same sequence length as the actual output tensor after packing/unpacking. Use the original mask on the embedded input rather than on the packed/unpacked output.

candidates.title: Initialize optimizer before training loop to avoid NameError
candidates.action: Define the optimizer outside the epoch loop, ensuring it is always available even when no stage transition occurs.

candidates.title: Use progressive unfreezing with discriminative learning rates and stochastic depth for transformer fine-tuning
candidates.action: Gradually unfreeze transformer layers from top to bottom, applying lower learning rates to lower layers. Use stochastic depth regularization on top layers. Train with AdamW optimizer, linear warmup, and early stopping.

candidates.title: Use combined loss with RMSE, SSIM, and edge-aware (Sobel) loss for denoising
candidates.action: Combine RMSE (or MSE), SSIM, and an edge-aware loss (e.g., L1 on Sobel gradients) to balance pixel accuracy, perceptual quality, and edge preservation.

candidates.title: Use CalibratedClassifierCV with estimator parameter in newer scikit-learn
candidates.action: When using CalibratedClassifierCV from scikit-learn >=1.0, use the parameter name 'estimator' instead of 'base_estimator' or 'base_engine'.
